text: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One understood the middle way of practice, which gives vision and knowledge, and leads to peace, direct knowledge, awakening, and extinguishment.
note: From the first discourse. The two extremes are indulgence in sensual pleasure and self-mortification.

text: Now this is the noble truth of suffering. Rebirth is suffering; old age is suffering; illness is suffering; death is suffering
right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.
This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.
It’s like a person who is struck with an arrow, only to be struck with a second arrow. That person experiences the feeling of two arrows.
note: The first arrow is the pain; the second is the distress added to it.

text: Mendicants, all is burning.
note: The fire sermon: burning with the fires of greed, hate and delusion.

text: Good friends, companions, and associates are the whole of the spiritual life.
note: Said to Ananda, who had called good friendship half of the spiritual life.

text: Looking after yourself, you look after others; and looking after others, you look after yourself.
there is much more that I have directly known but have not explained to you. What I have explained is a tiny amount.
note: Said holding a few leaves in a forest: he taught only what helps end suffering.

text: when you abuse, harass, and attack us who do not abuse, harass, and attack, we don’t accept it. It still belongs to you, brahmin, it still belongs to you!
note: Said to a brahmin who had come to insult him: a gift not accepted stays with the giver.

text: So too old age and death advance upon all living creatures
I will teach you a simile of the teaching as a raft: for crossing over, not for holding on.
Suppose a man was struck by an arrow thickly smeared with poison. His friends and colleagues, relatives and kin would get a surgeon to treat him.
note: The man refuses treatment until he knows who shot him; he would die first. So with speculative questions.

text: Even if low-down bandits were to sever you limb from limb with a two-handed saw, anyone who had a malevolent thought on that account would not be following my instructions.
deeds of body, speech, and mind should be done only after repeated checking.
note: Said to his son Rahula, comparing reflection to a mirror.

text: Don’t run back to the past, don’t anticipate the future. What’s past is left behind, the future has not arrived
Please, Kālāmas, don’t go by oral transmission, don’t go by lineage, don’t go by testament, don’t go by canonical authority, don’t rely on logic, don’t rely on inference
note: The list continues, and the test he gives is not personal preference: see the next passage.

text: But when you know for yourselves: ‘These things are unskillful, blameworthy, criticized by sensible people, and when you undertake them, they lead to harm and suffering’, then you should give them up.

There is a question that should be answered categorically. There is a question that should be answered analytically. There is a question that should be answered with a counter-question. There is a question that should be set aside.
I am liable to grow old, I am not exempt from old age.
note: The first of five subjects he says everyone should often review.

text: I am the owner of my deeds and heir to my deeds.
It is speech that is timely, true, gentle, beneficial, and loving.
when energy is too forceful it leads to restlessness. When energy is too slack it leads to laziness.
note: Said to Sona, a former musician, after asking him about harp strings tuned too tight and too slack.

text: Gain and loss, fame and disgrace, blame and praise, pleasure and pain.
Conditions fall apart. Persist with diligence.
note: Said shortly before his death, and again as his last words.

text: live as your own island, your own refuge, with no other refuge.
note: Said to Ananda. He goes on: let the teaching be your island and your refuge.

text: the helper, the friend in good times and bad, the counselor, and the one who’s sympathetic.
note: The four good-hearted friends, from his advice to the householder Sigalaka.

text: Even as a mother would protect with her life her child, her only child, so too for all creatures unfold a boundless heart.
May they be happy and safe! May all beings be happy!
Not to fraternize with fools, but to fraternize with the wise, and honoring those worthy of honor: this is the highest blessing.
As clay pots made by a potter all end up being broken, so is the life of mortals.
In the seen will be merely the seen; in the heard will be merely the heard
Intention is the leader of things; intention is first, they’re made by intention.
For never is hatred laid to rest by hate, it’s laid to rest by love: this is an ancient teaching.
it’s good to tame the mind; a tamed mind leads to bliss.
Don’t find fault with others, with what they’ve done or left undone.
As the wind cannot stir a solid mass of rock, so too blame and praise do not affect the wise.
Better than a thousand meaningless sayings is a single meaningful saying, hearing which brings you peace.
The supreme conqueror is not he who conquers a million men in battle, but he who conquers a single man: himself.
All tremble at the rod, all fear death. Treating others like oneself, neither kill nor incite to kill.
One is indeed the lord of oneself, for who else would be one’s lord?
Not to do any evil; to embrace the good; to purify one’s mind: this is the instruction of the Buddhas.
Health is the ultimate blessing; contentment, the ultimate wealth
Defeat anger with kindness, villainy with virtue, stinginess with giving, and lies with truth.
It’s easy to see the faults of others, hard to see one’s own.
You yourselves must do the work, the Realized Ones just show the way.
All conditions are impermanent— when this is seen with wisdom, one grows disillusioned with suffering: this is the path to purity.
